# HYBE Executives Land 30th in Billboard's 2026 Power 100

Multi-home, multi-genre strategy and global influence recognized in Leaderboard category

By OSEN

Published 2026.01.29. 09:39

0

[OSEN=Choi Lee-jung Reporter] HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk, HYBE CEO Lee Jae-sang, and HYBE America Chairman and CEO Isaac Lee were all named to ‘Billboard’s 2026 Power 100.’

The U.S. music media outlet Billboard announced the list of the world’s most influential figures in the music industry, ‘Billboard’s 2026 Power 100,’ on its official website on the 28th (local time). This year’s list featured Chairman Bang, CEO Lee, and Chairman and CEO Isaac Lee in the ‘Leaderboard’ category, which recognizes 40 leaders who have significantly impacted the global music industry, ranking them jointly at 30th place. This reaffirms HYBE’s strong presence in the global entertainment market.

Billboard described HYBE, stating, “Through its ‘multi-home, multi-genre’ strategy, it has established overseas bases and utilized K-pop-style artist and fandom development methods in the global market.” Chairman Bang and the other two HYBE executives were also ranked 5th in the ‘Multisector’ category, which comprehensively evaluates influence across various aspects of music production and consumption, including management and performances.

Chairman Bang has been selected for the list six times, including this year, following his appearances in 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025. Billboard highlighted, “HYBE does not merely export artists produced in Korea to overseas markets, including the U.S.,” and praised Chairman Bang’s K-pop methodology for establishing itself as a localized success model in major global markets.

Notably, Billboard mentioned that KATSEYE, a global girl group applying Chairman Bang’s K-pop methodology, “was nominated for ‘Best New Artist’ at the Grammys through a collaboration with Geffen Records.” KATSEYE also received a simultaneous nomination in the ‘Best Pop Duo/Group Performance’ category, solidifying its position as a global leading group.

CEO Lee Jae-sang and Chairman and CEO Isaac Lee, who were named to the list for the first time this year, also drew attention. This is interpreted as recognition of their achievements in securing future growth engines for HYBE and advancing its global business.

CEO Lee has led the ‘HYBE 2.0’ strategy, driving preemptive innovation in the industry by integrating content and technology, and has provided fans with new immersive experiences. He also accelerated the ‘multi-home, multi-genre’ strategy by establishing HYBE China and HYBE India last year. Thanks to these achievements, he was selected as one of the most influential entertainment executives worldwide by Billboard’s 2025 Power Players and Variety, a U.S. entertainment magazine.

Billboard noted, “HYBE established regional bases in China and India, the two most populous countries in the world,” and highlighted the achievements of HYBE Music Group artists, including SEVENTEEN’s regular 5th album ‘HAPPY BURSTDAY’ topping the Billboard Top Album Sales chart last year, and Tomorrow X Together and ENHYPEN ranking 3rd on the Billboard 200.

Chairman and CEO Isaac Lee has contributed to expanding HYBE’s musical territory by leading its global strategy in the North American and Latin markets. Billboard highlighted his achievement, stating, “In Latin America, he created the boy band Santos Bravos through a reality series.” Santos Bravos, which debuted in October last year following the reality series of the same name, is evaluated as a successful fusion of the K-pop system and Latin pop. Chairman and CEO Isaac Lee was also selected for Billboard’s Latin Power Players 2025 last year.

Meanwhile, Billboard’s Power 100 is an annual list published by Billboard recognizing influential figures in the global music industry, selecting leaders in categories such as labels, publishing, and multisector. This year’s list also included Lucian Grainge, CEO of UMG (Universal Music Group), Rob Stringer, Chairman of Sony Music Group, and Michael Rapino, Chairman of Live Nation.

title: Lee Jae-sang, CEO of Hybe: “2026 Will Be the Year HYBE 2.0 ...
content:
Lee Jae-sang, CEO of Hybe, stated this in his New Year’s address on the 2nd, indicating that this year will be a turning point where the HYBE 2.0 strategy begins to yield tangible results. He noted, “For us, 2025 was a time to strengthen our company’s capacity for sustainable growth through strategic investments and internal consolidation.” He emphasized, “This year, we will demonstrate to the market that our bold, proactive investments were the right choice and that the time spent improving our fundamentals was worthwhile.” [...] He also presented five key tasks for all members to achieve together this year: verifying the business potential of new ventures and Intellectual Property (IP); establishing the sustainability of IP and expanding the fan base through ‘unexplored innovation’; designing new experience models based on scarcity; securing leadership in the AI-driven prosumer market; and realizing true global governance.

First, Lee stressed the need to prove the validity of proactive investments made in new businesses and artist IP. He explained, “We have already seen significant traffic growth, and now we must shift to generating meaningful revenue to ensure sustainable business. When investments yield results, new investments gain legitimacy and a virtuous cycle of growth is established.” [...] He also highlighted the importance of securing leadership in the prosumer market, where fans and users directly create and share content. Lee stated, “It is necessary to apply integrated and concrete response models from both creative and platform perspectives. By proactively protecting the value of IP and establishing a Fan to Fan model that allows fans to freely create and communicate, we can set the standard for the market.”

Regarding future global strategies, he said, “We will build integrated global governance that organically shares key assets and know-how—such as resources, talent, and content distribution—among global subsidiaries. This will increase cross-border project cases and realize true global synergy.”

Lee Jae-sang, CEO of Hybe. Photo courtesy of Hybe

“If 2025 was a year of ‘investment’ to lay the strategic foundation for HYBE 2.0, then 2026 will mark the beginning of ‘realization’ where those achievements become visible.”

Lee Jae-sang, CEO of Hybe, stated this in his New Year’s address on the 2nd, indicating that this year will be a turning point where the HYBE 2.0 strategy begins to yield tangible results. He noted, “For us, 2025 was a time to strengthen our company’s capacity for sustainable growth through strategic investments and internal consolidation.” He emphasized, “This year, we will demonstrate to the market that our bold, proactive investments were the right choice and that the time spent improving our fundamentals was worthwhile.”

He also presented five key tasks for all members to achieve together this year: verifying the business potential of new ventures and Intellectual Property (IP); establishing the sustainability of IP and expanding the fan base through ‘unexplored innovation’; designing new experience models based on scarcity; securing leadership in the AI-driven prosumer market; and realizing true global governance.

First, Lee stressed the need to prove the validity of proactive investments made in new businesses and artist IP. He explained, “We have already seen significant traffic growth, and now we must shift to generating meaningful revenue to ensure sustainable business. When investments yield results, new investments gain legitimacy and a virtuous cycle of growth is established.”

He continued, “The essence of Hybe’s business lies in achieving proactive innovation by merging content and technology based on the core IP of music and artists. Through this, we provide fans with new immersive experiences. This approach lays the foundation for Hybe artists to maintain unique, high-quality, and sustainable IP, regardless of changes in the environment.”

He further emphasized the need to design new experience models based on scarcity. Lee said, “Scarcity is a key factor that can enhance the added value of fandom business and fan experiences. Just as in the past, 2026 will be a crucial year for Hybe to design and test integrated online and offline experience models based on scarcity, driving innovation in the future music fandom business model.”

He also highlighted the importance of securing leadership in the prosumer market, where fans and users directly create and share content. Lee stated, “It is necessary to apply integrated and concrete response models from both creative and platform perspectives. By proactively protecting the value of IP and establishing a Fan to Fan model that allows fans to freely create and communicate, we can set the standard for the market.”

Regarding future global strategies, he said, “We will build integrated global governance that organically shares key assets and know-how—such as resources, talent, and content distribution—among global subsidiaries. This will increase cross-border project cases and realize true global synergy.”

Finally, Lee concluded, “Hybe’s growth philosophy is clear: to create top-tier IP, lead the fandom business, and expand those achievements into new markets and genres. The protagonists of this journey are all of us. I hope every member of Hybe will become both the driving force and partner in our growth.”

# Jaesang Lee, CEO of HYBE: "2026 Marks the First Year of 'HYBE 2.0' Results Realization"

by **Lee Yiseul**

**Pubilshed** 02 Jan.2026 10:45(KST)

### Five Key Focus Areas Announced in New Year's Address

![Jaesang Lee, CEO of HYBE: "2026 Marks the First Year of 'HYBE 2.0' Results Realization"](https://cphoto.asiae.co.kr/listimglink/1/2026010210351576564_1767317715.jpg)

Jaesang Lee, CEO of HYBE, declared 2026 as the year of 'realization' in his New Year's address on January 2. He expressed his intention to begin full-scale profit generation, building on the foundation of the 'HYBE 2.0' strategy established last year.

CEO Lee emphasized, "If 2025 was a year of investment to lay the groundwork for 'HYBE 2.0,' then 2026 will mark the beginning of visible results. This year, we will prove to the market that our bold investments were the right direction."

On this day, Lee announced five key tasks that HYBE must accomplish: ▲Verifying the business potential of new businesses and intellectual property (IP) ▲Establishing the sustainability of IP and expanding the fan base ▲Designing a new experience model based on scarcity ▲Securing leadership in the AI-based prosumer market ▲Implementing true global governance.

He identified securing profitability as the top priority. CEO Lee explained, "While we have confirmed significant traffic expansion in new businesses, we must now shift to a phase of generating meaningful profit. A virtuous cycle of investment will be established only when we are confident in sustainable business potential."

He further stated, "The essence of HYBE's business is to provide fans with new immersive experiences through the convergence of technology based on core IP. We will lay the groundwork for artists to continue as unique IPs despite changes in the environment."

In the fandom business sector, he presented 'scarcity' as the core keyword. CEO Lee said, "Scarcity is an important element that enhances the added value of the fan experience. To innovate future fandom businesses, we will design and test an integrated online and offline experience model based on scarcity."

He added, "It is necessary to apply an integrated and concrete response model from both creative and platform perspectives. While preserving the value of IP, we will establish a 'Fan to Fan' model where fans can freely create and communicate, setting a new standard for the market."

Regarding global strategy, he emphasized building 'integrated governance' between headquarters and overseas subsidiaries. CEO Lee explained, "We will increase cross-border project cases and realize greater synergy."

He concluded, "HYBE's growth philosophy is to create top-level IP, lead the fandom business, and expand into new markets. I ask every member to take ownership of this growth."

# Hybe leaders named to Billboard’s 2026 Power 100 list

Published : Jan. 29, 2026 - 16:16:24 Updated : Jan. 30, 2026 - 18:13:34

* + Link copied!



*Lee Jung-joo* 

Covering K-pop issues,  
trends

Hybe’s top executives — chairman Bang Si-hyuk, CEO Lee Jae-sang and Hybe America chairman and CEO Isaac Lee — have been named among the most influential figures in the global music industry, according to Billboard’s 2026 Power 100 list released Wednesday.

Billboard annually selects key leaders across the global music ecosystem for its Power 100 list, recognizing those driving innovation across sectors such as labels, publishing, live performance and multi-sector leadership. The three leaders of Hybe were jointly listed at No. 30 on this year’s “Leaderboard” — a category spotlighting 40 global executives who are reshaping the music business.

Billboard praised Hybe’s “multihome, multigenre” strategy, highlighting how the company has successfully established international agencies while applying its K-pop-style artist and fandom development model to the global music market. It spotlighted Katesye — Hybe’s girl group co-developed with Geffen Records — as a prime example of that approach, noting the group’s Grammy nomination for Best New Artist.

Bang’s presence on the list marks his sixth appearance overall, having previously been selected in 2020 and consecutively from 2022 to 2025.

CEO Lee Jae-sang and Hybe America head Isaac Lee marked their first appearance on the Power 100 this year, recognized for leading Hybe’s global expansion as well as identifying future growth engines.

Lee Jae-sang, who spearheaded Hybe’s “Hybe 2.0” strategy, was credited for integrating content and technology to create new fan engagement experiences. CEO Lee was also acknowledged for playing a key role in the launch of Hybe China and Hybe India, accelerating the company’s multi-market strategy.

Billboard noted the strategic importance of establishing regional headquarters in the world’s two most populous countries, adding that Hybe artists Seventeen, Tomorrow X Together and Enhypen have all found success on the Billboard charts. According to Hybe, Seventeen topped the Top Album Sales chart with their fifth album, “Happy Burstday,” while Tomorrow X Together and Enhypen each reached No. 3 on the Billboard 200.

Hybe America CEO and chairman Isaac Lee was spotlighted for leading Hybe’s North American and Latin American expansion. Billboard noted that the company launched the boy band Santos Bravos through a Latin American reality series — a hybrid model combining K-pop production systems with Latin pop.

In addition to their appearance on the Leaderboard, the three Hybe executives also ranked fifth in the “Multisector” category, which evaluates influence across various parts of music-making and consumption — such as artist management and live entertainment.

Other executives named to this year’s Billboard Power 100 list include chairman and CEO Lucian Grainge of Universal Music Group, chairman Rob Stringer of Sony Music Group and president and CEO Michael Rapino of Live Nation.

She will also play a key role in expanding Hybe America’s presence in Atlanta—her hometown and a global epicenter of R&B and hip-hop.

“Ethiopia is a once-in-a-generation leader whose impact on artists, songwriters, culture, and the music business is undeniable,” shares Isaac Lee, Chairman & CEO of Hybe America. “Her vision, taste, and strategic insight make her uniquely suited to help shape the next chapter of Hybe America as we continue building a future-facing entertainment company centered on artists and fans.”

# Hybe America Staffs Up for 2026—Ethiopia Habtemariam Named President of Music

![Hybe America staffing hires 2026](https://www.digitalmusicnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/hybe-america-ethiopia-habtemariam-1024x576.jpg)

Photo Credit: Hybe America (Ethiopia Habtemariam)

Photo Credit: Hybe America (Ethiopia Habtemariam)

## Hybe America has announced several new staff appointments as 2026 rolls onward. Ethiopia Habtemariam has been appointed as President of Music, while PR vet Johanna Fuentes is joining as Executive VP and Head of Communications & Public Relations. Here’s the latest.

Habtemariam will help advance [Hybe America’s long-term growth strategy](https://www.digitalmusicnews.com/2025/05/28/hybe-america-sells-big-machine-rock/), spearheading A&R and artist development initiatives across the company’s label ecosystem and identifying new creative and commercial opportunities at the intersection of music, culture, and fandom. She will also play a key role in expanding Hybe America’s presence in Atlanta—her hometown and a global epicenter of R&B and hip-hop.

“Ethiopia is a once-in-a-generation leader whose impact on artists, songwriters, culture, and the music business is undeniable,” [shares](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/hybe-america-appoints-ethiopia-habtemariam-162800923.html) Isaac Lee, Chairman & CEO of Hybe America. “Her vision, taste, and strategic insight make her uniquely suited to help shape the next chapter of Hybe America as we continue building a future-facing entertainment company centered on artists and fans.”

#### Habtemariam’s career has been defined by artist and songwriter-first leadership, cultural fluency, and the ability to build and scale enduring creative businesses. Most recently, she served as Chairwoman and CEO of Motown Records, where she led the iconic label through a period of revitalization and growth, championing both emerging and established artists while expanding Motown’s global reach.

During her tenure, she spearheaded the landmark Quality Control-Motown label venture, overseeing the signing and development of genre-defining artists including Lil Yachty, City Girls, Migos, and Lil Baby while also signing and championing artists such as Leon Thomas and NBA YoungBoy.

Meanwhile, PR vet Johanna Fuentes [joins](https://variety.com/2026/music/news/johanna-fuentes-hybe-america-head-of-communications-pr-1236626212/) Hybe America as Executive VP and Head of Communications and Public Relations. In this newly created role, she’ll handle all internal and external communications for Hybe across North and South America. Fuentes will be based in Los Angeles and will work with Hybe America’s senior leadership team as well as Hybe’s global PR team in South Korea.
